power_up_sequence: Ramp VDDC, VDDQ, VDDQL, VPP with RESET_n LOW.
Deassert RESET_n once supplies and clocks are stable.
Program per-channel mode registers and train links before normal operation.

low_power_modes_summary.power_down: Per-channel power-down with fast exit; channel clock may be gated.
low_power_modes_summary.self_refresh: DRAM self-refreshes; channel clock may stop; exit re-synchronizes.
low_power_modes_summary.temperature_compensated_refresh: Refresh rate adapted using TEMP to save power while preserving retention.

dvfs_summary.DVFSC: Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling Core — selects VDD2H or VDD2L to scale core voltage with frequency.
dvfs_summary.DVFSQ: Scales the DQ-domain voltage / Vref(dq) with the FSP.
dvfs_summary.FSP: Frequency Set Points (FSP-OP / FSP-WR) hold per-frequency RL/WL/ODT/Vref/DFE, switched on a DVFS change.

fields.notes: DDR5's power intent centers on the on-module PMIC generating 1.1 V / 1.8 V rails from 12 V, the 1.1 V VDD/VDDQ operating point, CKE power-down and self-refresh states, and refresh-management options. Fine-grained power-domain partitioning of the DRAM die is a vendor concern.

power_domains_summary.purpose: Low-swing supply for the high-speed links.
Elevated supply for wordline boost / array operation.

fields.power_efficiency_rationale: HBM achieves higher bandwidth than DDR4/GDDR5 while using less power and a smaller form factor by stacking dies and using a wide, low-swing, short interposer interface. Separate IO / low-swing rails (VDDQ/VDDQL) reduce IO energy per bit at 6.4 Gb/s/pin.
fields.thermal_note: Stacked dies under sustained high bandwidth concentrate heat; the host system provides cooling and uses TEMP to manage refresh and throttling. Removing the buffer/base die can lower cost and power at the expense of bandwidth (a separate low-cost HBM direction); standard HBM3 retains the base/logic die.

power_management_states.name: Active
power_management_states.description: Device trained and servicing commands on both sub-channels.

fields.wakeup_mechanism: CKE controls power-down entry/exit; SELF REFRESH ENTRY/EXIT controls the low-power retention state. Exit returns to active operation; at high speed bins some re-training may be required.

power_rails.purpose: Core supply (on a DIMM, generated by the on-module PMIC from 12 V).

fields.dimm_pmic: DDR5 moves power management onto the DIMM: an on-module Power Management IC (PMIC) regulates the 12 V host supply down to the 1.1 V VDD/VDDQ and 1.8 V VPP rails locally, improving rail integrity and per-DIMM power control (DDR4 DIMMs had no on-module PMIC).
fields.ddr5_power_considerations: Lower 1.1 V VDD/VDDQ (vs DDR4's 1.2 V) reduces dynamic and IO power; the on-module PMIC, fine-granularity / temperature-controlled refresh, same-bank refresh, power-down, and self-refresh manage energy; on-die ECC trades a little power for reliability.

extraction_hints: Look for power-domain partitioning, supply nets.
